provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — anomalous logons to central OT-management/support servers (new source, off-hours, privileged) are detectable via identity/authentication analytics where such logging exists

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: high — wscript/cscript executing a .vbs that spawns batch/archive-extraction and destructive utilities is a high-fidelity process-lineage detection

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: high — cmd.exe executing this specific named batch chain, mutex file __lock6423900.dat, and rapid sequential invocation of vssadmin/bcdedit/wevtutil are strong host detections
high — PowerShell script-block logging captures Add-MpPreference exclusions and Disable-NetAdapter, which are anomalous immediately preceding wiper execution
medium — wmic invocations for shadowcopy deletion and domain removal are detectable via command-line telemetry but require correlation with the surrounding destructive sequence
high — creation of a scheduled task named 'mstask' timed for 23:55 (Event ID 4698) and deletion of 'AnalyzeAll' are actor-specific, high-fidelity signals

detection_candidates.technique_name: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification
detection_candidates.rationale: high — new/modified GPOs that stage scripts from SYSVOL or push scheduled tasks/startup scripts are detectable via directory-service change auditing and GPO monitoring (Event IDs 5136/5137, SYSVOL writes)
medium — scripted queries for installed AV products are detectable via command-line/registry-query telemetry but resemble benign inventory checks in isolation
high — creation of Defender exclusion paths (Add-MpPreference) is a strong, uncommon signal captured by EDR tamper telemetry and PowerShell logging
high — wevtutil clear-log invocations and Event ID 1102 (Security log cleared) are high-fidelity, especially clustered with wiper activity
medium — deletion of just-executed binaries is detectable via file-delete + preceding-execution correlation, but the surrounding wipe destroys much of the evidence

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — extraction of password-protected RARs by a script and high-entropy config files are detectable via file-write/entropy and command-line telemetry
medium — registry writes to lock-screen/boot/screensaver keys by a non-standard process are detectable via registry-modification telemetry when clustered with the wipe
medium — 'ms*'-style names in unusual paths executing destructive utilities are detectable via name/path/hash baselining and signature-vs-name mismatch
medium — reads of a .cab from SYSVOL followed by local RAR extraction are detectable via file-access and process telemetry, but resemble software distribution
medium — bulk local file collection is detectable via file-access/staging patterns but is common; value comes from process-lineage context
medium — bulk mailbox/email export is detectable via mail-server access and export auditing where available
high — mass file overwrite/deletion by a single process is high-signal on host/EDR telemetry (rapid file-modification bursts, mass MFT changes)
high — raw writes to \\.\PhysicalDrive0 / sector 0 (MBR) by a user-mode process are rare and high-fidelity on host telemetry
high — vssadmin/wmic shadow deletion and bcdedit boot-record tampering are classic, high-fidelity pre-impact detections
medium — unauthorized content changes on internal signage/HMI systems are observable where those systems are logged/monitored, but such OT signage often lacks telemetry

high — anomalous HMI/PLC commands and out-of-envelope process setpoints are high-signal on OT/ICS historian, engineering-workstation and safety-system telemetry, though such OT visibility is frequently absent in practice
medium — service/adapter disablement is detectable on affected hosts, but the fuel-pump control layer is OT-side and often under-instrumented
medium — a non-standard process replacing the lock screen/wallpaper and forcing logoff is detectable on host telemetry when clustered with the wipe sequence
high — mass password changes, forced domain unjoin, and bulk session logoff across hosts are anomalous, high-signal events on identity/host telemetry
medium — forced reboot/shutdown following boot-record tampering is detectable but is the final step after higher-signal precursors

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — pre-intrusion knowledge is inferred from later artifacts and is not itself endpoint-observable; intel/hunt candidate
low — capability development occurs off-victim; intel candidate for tooling attribution
low — actor-controlled social channels are off-victim; brand/OSINT-monitoring candidate
low — trust-relationship abuse via a third-party management platform is largely invisible to the downstream victim; hunt/intel candidate at the provider tier
low — process enumeration by the wiper is transient and immediately followed by destruction; limited standalone signal
low — OS-version checks are ubiquitous and benign in isolation
low — publication occurs off-victim via web/messaging services; intel/leak-monitoring candidate
low — the on-chain burn and destructive banking actions are largely observed off-victim (chain analysis, victim disclosure); intel candidate
